verdict.rationale: Testing in a sandbox is a fair question for a self-hosted AI platform, but the evidence shows no product-provided sandbox or test environment isolated from production data. The 'auto' approval mode is a dry-run/approval gate, not sandbox isolation. Per-task worktrees isolate code changes, not production data. The dev-mode Swagger UI is an API docs surface, not a test environment. Running a separate self-hosted instance would be a user-side workaround. missing for 10: a documented sandbox/staging environment, isolation of test runs from production data, and evidence that agent or API testing can target that sandbox.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: auto is the everyday setting: the AI can explore freely, but nothing changes on disk and no command runs until you say so.
one worktree per task, one workspace per worktree, one agent per workspace, all supervised from a single browser tab.
